expected_level_description: You can: - align your work with the work being done by other architects and technical professionals - track emerging issues, strategies, roadmaps, patterns and technologies over time to assess opportunities and risks to your work - identify how other teams contribute to delivering outcomes through change

You can: - listen to the needs of technical and business stakeholders - create and use different architecture representations to communicate effectively, achieving agreement with technical and non-technical stakeholders - provide support in discussions about architectural topics within a multidisciplinary team

You can: - contribute to the work of others - motivate and empower teams - create the right environment for teams to work in, and can identify the best team makeup depending on the situation - recognise and deal with issues

You can: - work with others to make architectural design decisions characterised by managed levels of risk and complexity - identify and address architectural risks relevant to your team or domain, for example, business, data, or security - engage with architectural governance and assurance to effectively manage decisions and risks, with support

You can: - support the development of a strategy or vision that aligns with organisational objectives - challenge requirements and assumptions, and identify opportunities to develop strategy - support the implementation of a strategy or vision, for example, by using a roadmap or plan - use architectural principles, patterns, and constraints when appropriate

skill: Technical design throughout the life cycle
expected_level_description: You can: - create technical designs characterised by managed levels of risk, impact, and complexity - provide guidance and support to teams using technical designs throughout the life cycle - adapt a technical design if needed during delivery - work with well-understood technology and identify appropriate patterns

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - read and use FHIR resources, profiles, and APIs - build or test simple integrations under guidance - check messages against a specification
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - follow access rules and protect your credentials
